_about: A SYNTHETIC export, hand-built for the test harness (docs/fix-plan-2026-09-28.md, R0). Not written by World Bible. It differs from Aurvantis on purpose: settlement kinds VILLAGE/TOWN/CITY match their scale; stock sentences use the settlement's own scale word; play.cast roles are real words; fact keys are the alternates (Terrain, Landscape, Daily Life, Customs, Conflict) rather than Geography / Biomes / Urban Life / Tension; two travel rows carry no miles and no crosses; Marrowby is a port; Oakhollow has no cast; Brindle Ford, Oakhollow, Caddonbury and Pellow Green ship no play.places.

world.name: Calvessa
world.secret: The pale moon is drawing the sea further inland every year.

facts.Cosmology: One sun, one pale moon, and a long grey sea around a single landmass
facts.Magic: Quiet hedge-craft and a few learned orders; nothing that moves mountains

sections.title: Cosmology
paragraphs: Calvessa has one sun and one pale moon, and the sea that rings its only landmass is grey in every season.
Its people reckon years from the Drowning, when the southern shore was lost to the sea.

facts.Terrain: chalk downs, beech hangers, slow clay rivers
facts.Landscape: rolling downland cut by river valleys, with salt marsh along the southern shore
facts.Climate: mild and wet, with hard westerly gales in winter

sections.title: Landscape
paragraphs: Lathwe is chalk downland folded into long valleys, each with a slow clay river at the bottom and beech woods hanging on the steep sides.
Along the southern shore the downs give way to salt marsh, creeks and mudflats that flood twice a day.

sections.title: Climate
paragraphs: The weather is mild and wet for most of the year; in winter the westerly gales come off the sea hard enough to strip thatch.

facts.Body: Stocky, broad-handed, weathered early by wind
facts.Homeland: the river valleys of the downs

sections.title: Body
paragraphs: The Fenwic are stocky and broad-handed, and the wind weathers their faces early.

facts.Homeland: the marsh shore and the creeks behind it
facts.Livelihood: Fishing, salt-panning and the carrying trade

sections.title: Body
paragraphs: The Carrow are tall and long-limbed, with dark eyes and a stooped way of walking learned in low boats.

facts.Governance: a council of valley reeves meeting at each quarter-day

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: The Wealdmark is governed by a council of valley reeves who meet at each quarter-day and agree on as little as they can.

facts.Governance: a compact of marsh towns under an elected warden
facts.Economy: salt, smoked fish and river carriage

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: The Saltholm Compact is a league of marsh towns that elect a warden every seven years and argue with every one of them.

entities.name: Brindle Ford
entities.summary: A ford village on the Brindle, a few hundred souls

facts.Landscape: water meadows either side of a gravel ford
facts.Daily Life: everyone turns out when the ford floods
facts.Governance: a village reeve answering to the valley council
facts.Conflict: who pays to keep the ford stones in place

sections.title: Daily Life
paragraphs: Brindle Ford is a village of flint cottages strung along a gravel ford, with water meadows on both banks.
The village's reeve is chosen from the village's own oldest families and answers to the valley council.
When the river rises everyone in the village turns out to shift the stepping stones before the current takes them.

entities.summary: A charcoal-burners' village in a wooded combe

facts.Landscape: a steep wooded combe with a stream at the bottom
facts.Daily Life: the clamps are watched day and night while they burn
facts.Governance: the oldest burner speaks for the village

sections.title: Daily Life
paragraphs: Oakhollow is a village of timber huts in a steep wooded combe, and the smoke of the charcoal clamps hangs over it in every season.
Nobody in the village keeps written records; the oldest burner speaks for everyone.

entities.name: Kestwick
entities.summary: A market town at the head of the valley

facts.Landscape: a chalk spur above the river crossing
facts.Daily Life: market day is Thursday and the whole valley comes in
facts.Customs: a stranger buys the first round
facts.Governance: a town reeve and a bench of guild wardens
facts.Conflict: the smiths and the wool merchants both want the market hall

sections.title: Daily Life
paragraphs: Kestwick is a market town of timber-framed houses on a chalk spur above the river crossing.
The town's reeve sits with a bench of guild wardens, and the town's smiths and wool merchants have quarrelled over the market hall for a generation.
On Thursdays the whole valley comes in to the town's market and the streets are impassable by noon.

entities.name: Marrowby
entities.summary: A fishing town on a marsh creek, with a harbour

facts.Landscape: a shingle spit at the mouth of a marsh creek
facts.Architecture: tarred weatherboard on stilts above the high-water mark
facts.Daily Life: the tide sets the working day, not the clock
facts.Conflict: the salt-pans are silting and nobody agrees whose dredging it is

sections.title: Daily Life
paragraphs: Marrowby is a fishing town of tarred weatherboard houses raised on stilts along a shingle spit at the mouth of a marsh creek.
The town's harbour court is made up of boat-owners, and the town's quay is where every quarrel ends up.
In Marrowby the tide sets the working day: the boats go out on the ebb and the whole town is on the quay when they come back.

entities.name: Caddonbury
entities.summary: The walled river city where the warden sits

facts.Landscape: a broad river bend inside old earth ramparts
facts.Architecture: stone halls, brick warehouses, and a cathedral of grey limestone
facts.Daily Life: the bells of the cathedral ring the hours for the whole city
facts.Customs: debts are settled on the cathedral steps
facts.Governance: the warden of the Compact and a city assembly of guilds
facts.Conflict: the river guilds and the warden's customs men

sections.title: Daily Life
paragraphs: Caddonbury is a walled city in a broad bend of the river, grown up inside old earth ramparts that no longer hold it.
The city's assembly of guilds sits beneath the warden of the Compact, and the city's river guilds fight the warden's customs men over every barge.
The cathedral bells ring the hours for the whole city, and debts in the city are settled on the cathedral steps.

entities.name: Pellow Green
entities.summary: A shepherds' village on the edge of the marsh

facts.Landscape: a green on the last dry ground before the marsh
facts.Daily Life: the flocks come in off the marsh at dusk
facts.Governance: a village moot on the green

sections.title: Daily Life
paragraphs: Pellow Green is a village of cob cottages round a common, on the last dry ground before the marsh begins.
The village moot meets on the green, and the village's flocks come in off the marsh at dusk.

chronology.name: The Drowning
chronology.summary: The southern shore was lost to the sea in one winter.
chronology.aftermath: The marsh towns moved inland and founded the Compact.

chronology.name: The Ford Stones Laid
chronology.summary: Brindle Ford's stepping stones were set by the valley council.

chronology.name: The Salt Quarrel
chronology.summary: Marrowby and Caddonbury came to blows over landing fees.

trade_routes.friction: Kestwick's merchants set the price and Brindle Ford resents it.
The burners want paying in coin; the village pays in barley.
Marrowby buys fleeces cheap in a wet year.
The warden's customs men tax every cart at the ramparts.
The river guilds and the harbour court both claim the landing fees.
The city's drapers buy through one broker.

factions.name: The River Guilds
factions.description: Bargemen and landing-masters who hold the river between Caddonbury and the sea.
factions.reach: Every landing on the Caddon river.
factions.aim: Landing fees paid to them, not to the warden
factions.weakness: They cannot agree among themselves who speaks for them.

unwritten.name: The Grey Warden
unwritten.why: A former warden of the Compact, spoken of in Marrowby as if still alive.
